reason: The cited evidence shows CeO2 supports enhancing activity/stability for HEA clusters (E1) and configurational disorder improving oxide catalyst performance (E2), but neither demonstrates a CeO2 overlayer deposited by ALD on a multi-element alloy, nor its protective mechanism against sintering/poisoning under the specified automotive exhaust conditions. The key premises about the ALD overlayer's specific protective and redox-mediating role on this catalyst are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: CeO2 overlayers can act as oxygen storage/release media and redox mediators
CeO2 overlayers can protect active metal sites from sintering
CeO2 overlayers can enhance catalytic activity and stability for NO reduction or CO oxidation
ALD can deposit conformal, ultra-thin (1-2 nm) CeO2 overlayers on catalyst nanoparticles
The proposed multi-element alloy catalyst benefits from a 'cocktail effect' for improved performance
